updates.title: A reproducible street-level comparison
updates.summary: The yellow saloon sign now gives us an identifiable static landmark in both the retail reference and Bevy. This is a manually fitted comparison camera, not original camera behavior.
changes: Added explicit inspection eye/target/FOV and physical viewport parameters, plus GPU-free projection tests.
Identified the saloon sign through its actual material-to-mesh association; kept texture inspection extracts private.
Preserved failed rear-facing and occluded trials, then captured a street-level view at 512 × 448 without cropping or retouching.
Published a new same-landmark pair while retaining the earlier unmatched overview and all original files.
updates.validation: 52 synthetic Rust tests and 24 Python tests pass; formatting and viewer compilation pass. Four linked Windows/Vulkan camera runs captured original PNGs and exited at their 10-second limits. Invalid, incomplete, nonfinite and oversized camera/viewport inputs were rejected before opening a disc. A fifth run through the scripted workflow repeated the final pose with byte-identical PNG output on this setup.
updates.limits: The camera was manually fitted around one facade. Neighboring-wall parallax, colors, shadows, sky and actors still differ. Original game camera, complete scene activation and general transform/material parity remain unverified. No image-quality percentage or gameplay result is claimed.

link.label: Camera contract, landmark evidence and remaining discrepancies

updates.title: Placing real retail resources — diagnostic only
updates.summary: The Bevy viewer can now assemble a candidate town layout from the ISO. The first reference/Bevy pair is published in the comparison section, explicitly unmatched: gameplay camera versus overhead inspection.
changes: Specified and tested six explicit affine rotation sequences; multiaxis nodes without an order are refused, not guessed.
Reproduced all geometry counts on three retail candidates. An explicit r100 subset renders 148 nodes and 23,288 triangles.
Rejected an occluded desktop capture, then added direct framebuffer PNG capture. The all-resource view exposed a sky-rendering problem; manual exclusions remain clearly logged.
Recaptured the first-fight reference without a window. Published its unchanged PPM with a lossless PNG preview, alongside the original Bevy PNG.
updates.validation: 48 synthetic Rust tests and 24 Python tests pass. The linked Windows/Vulkan viewer saved its own framebuffer and exited normally after 30 seconds. The reference run exited normally at its planned frame limit; local comparison verified that the PNG preview preserves every original PPM RGB sample.
updates.limits: This is not a playable scene or a fidelity pass. Camera/scene alignment is unmatched, sky/material state is unresolved, and diagnostic exclusions are not game visibility rules. Rotation composition and units remain hypotheses. No actors, HUD, collision or gameplay are implemented.

link.label: Placement experiments, failed attempts and next comparison

updates.title: Keeping a resumable record and original comparisons
updates.summary: Progress now has a persistent checkpoint protocol. Selected reference and Bevy screenshots can be published together, unchanged, with provenance and explicit differences.
changes: Added resume instructions and a public progress record, separating observed results, hypotheses and missing evidence.
Added byte-preserving preparation of explicitly reviewed original PNG pairs, content-addressed names and hash/provenance checks.
Prepared a simple Reference / Bevy layout with links to each full-resolution original; no promotional counters or generated substitute images.
updates.validation: 22 synthetic Python tests pass, including pair preparation without source modification, hash/CRC/dimension checks, profile separation, review requirements, duplicate rejection and escaped HTML. The baseline Rust code is unchanged; its 38 tests and viewer compilation were rechecked.
updates.limits: No new engine feature or fidelity result. The gallery has no pairs yet: the current isolated prop and first-fight screenshots are not a matched comparison. A same-subject reference capture is still required. The owner publication request does not license game imagery under MIT.

updates.title: A first real static prop in Bevy
updates.summary: A well-like prop from the retail ISO now renders with its referenced textures. This is an isolated asset view; a room and its gameplay are still not reconstructed.
changes: Added bounded static MDB geometry, explicit triangle winding and checked TM3 texture-bank binding.
Decoded 433 meshes and 158 bank images on three candidates; counts match the private probes.
Displayed the selected prop with five mesh buffers and five actual textures, in local coordinates with unlit materials.
Checked the direct GS texture-address mapper against independent synthetic table-reference images; game screenshots stay private.
updates.validation: 38 synthetic Rust tests pass. The linked Windows/Vulkan viewer was visually inspected and exited normally after 60 seconds. Full room placement, game lighting and reference-runtime visual parity are not established.
updates.limits: The view uses nearest/repeat sampling, two-sided diagnostic rendering and alpha blending. Vertex colors, GS alpha tests, camera behavior and scene transforms remain future fidelity work. Static flag-zero and observed indexed-texture profiles only.

link.label: Static-mesh evidence, scope and next comparison

updates.title: Reading room containers and node references
updates.summary: The reader can now navigate room-candidate storage and inspect node metadata without extracting the archive. No room is rendered yet.
changes: Checked 94 outer DAT catalogs, 93 nonempty SCP children and 1,708 nested storage sections directly from the retail ISO.
Validated SCR metadata on three candidates: 156, 232 and 45 nodes, including backward MDB references and finite raw transforms.
Corroborated data-layout observations with Chihuahua’s independent MIT format research; documented failed assumptions about sizes and alignment.
updates.validation: 29 synthetic Rust tests pass. Python and Rust agree on catalog/node counts. Nested member reads are bounded; signatures, ranges, overlap and malformed metadata are checked.
updates.limits: An MDB signature does not prove a valid mesh. Geometry, topology, UV/material association and transform composition are still unimplemented. Candidate room identity and prototype transfer remain unverified.

link.label: Room-data findings, validation and next experiment

updates.title: From archive entries to a first texture
updates.summary: The Rust reader now connects file paths to archive entries and displays a small texture directly from the owned ISO. This is an asset-reading step; no game scene is reconstructed yet.
changes: Mapped all 1,445 retail file records to AFS entries. Checked the prototype separately: 1,078 records, including empty-directory differences.
Added an original narrow TIM2 decoder: 34 top-level textures decode; one multi-palette font is explicitly refused.
Displayed 4-bit and 8-bit ISO textures in a separate Bevy inspection window. The interface-like image appears to be a retained mockup, so it is not counted as a recreated retail menu.
Wrote a first data map and ordered the next experiments around real room data. Parallel work waits for tested component contracts.
updates.validation: 22 synthetic Rust tests pass. Both reference catalogs validate. Real 4-bit/8-bit Bevy windows were visually inspected and exited at their 30/60-second deadlines. Game images and full inventories remain private.
updates.limits: No room geometry, animation, collision or gameplay is implemented. Reference-runtime palette/blending parity and prototype debug access remain unverified. REA rejected FST as unsupported; format observations came from a read-only local probe, not successful REA analysis.

link.label: Data map, evidence and next fidelity experiments

updates.title: Starting the Rust foundation loop
updates.summary: The first milestone now has executable steps and a decision log. The Rust sandbox renders original primitives, and read-only archive inspection can list catalog metadata.
changes: Added Doctor, Check, Build, Inspect, Catalog and bounded Smoke commands.
Verified a native Windows/Vulkan floor-and-capsule scene after fixing its tonemapping configuration.
Read the retail AFS catalog without extraction; added bounds and malformed-input tests.
Registered the June prototype as a separate observation profile and prepared an ignored corrected CUE.
updates.validation: 14 Rust synthetic tests and 12 Python tests pass locally. The sandbox reached its 45/60-second smoke deadlines and exited normally. Retail catalog inspection reports 1,445 entries; the original ISO hash matches its earlier baseline.
updates.limits: Original primitives only: no God Hand scene or game logic. FST/payload decoding and prototype debug-menu validation remain open. A Windows compiler crash was bypassed with one job and debug info disabled; its root cause is unknown.

updates.summary: The repository documentation, roadmap and development journal now use English. Conversations with the project owner remain in French.
changes: Translated public documentation and existing journal entries without changing task status.
Added a note explaining native backend outputs and how they can support independent development.
updates.validation: Regenerated the roadmap and journal; checked the public file boundary and reviewed the English page.

updates.title: First ps2-native-recomp trial
updates.summary: The third-party backend built from our ISO reaches God Hand’s first fight. This is a ps2-native-recomp result, not a Rust/Bevy engine result.
changes: Built the local runner without changing backend sources.
Observed the title, cinematic and first fight.
Saved and reloaded a runtime state; continued with scripted input.
updates.validation: One windowed trial covered 7,200 frames in 122.44 seconds. A second checked normal multithreaded mode and state creation. Resume continued to its planned frame limit.
updates.limits: Short trial only; casino and full game unverified. Pause, physical controller and native game saves remain untested. Gameplay captures, data and translations stay local.

updates.title: Repository published
updates.summary: The code and this journal are public on GitHub. The roadmap describes intended work, not features already available.
changes: Original source under MIT with provenance rules.
Published the journal on free GitHub Pages without progress counters or game assets.
updates.validation: GitHub checks passed: synthetic tests, formatting, Bevy compilation on Ubuntu and public-file validation. Reviewed the published page in the browser.
updates.limits: There is no independent-engine gameplay result. The graphical sandbox has only been compile-checked.

updates.title: First engine files
updates.summary: The repository contains a small read-only ISO reader and initial Rust foundations. No game logic runs in it yet.
changes: ISO 9660 root access and USA disc recognition.
Tests using synthetic images without game files.
Prepared a Bevy sandbox with a floor and capsule.
Simple development journal without progress statistics.
updates.validation: Rust tests and Bevy viewer compilation checked on Windows GNU. The reader recognizes the local ISO: GODHAND volume, six root entries.
updates.limits: The viewer was not run. No game scene, animation or logic is loaded.

updates.title: Choosing the direction
updates.summary: The initial idea was a PS2 recompilation port. After reviewing existing projects, the choice is to try an independent reimplementation in Rust and Bevy.
changes: The engine will use original public MIT code.
Game data stays in each user’s own ISO.
Observations and specifications must be separated from implementation.
updates.validation: Reviewed PS2Recomp, ps2-web-recomp and ps2-native-recomp as research references.
updates.limits: God Hand compatibility reported by ps2-native-recomp is not our engine’s result. Game logic and formats still need to be understood.

comparisons.title: A common saloon landmark at street level
comparisons.scenario: Retail frame 4501 and the same yellow saloon sign in candidate r100. The Bevy camera is manually fitted: eye (1.3, 2.6, 16), target (3.55, -1, -11.3), vertical FOV 45 degrees, 512 × 448 physical pixels. This is not the recovered gameplay camera.

reference.caption: Retail first fight, frame 4501; street-level reference

bevy.caption: Same saloon facade; explicit manually fitted inspection camera, unlit

observations: The sign and its supporting facade are identified through the actual ISO material/mesh association, then seen in both rendered outputs.
Both full frames retain their original 512 × 448 dimensions; no crop, warp or image retouching was used to align them.
The street-level view is a more useful comparison than the earlier overhead view; the earlier unmatched pair remains unchanged below.
limits: The pose was manually fitted around one facade. It does not prove the original camera, pixel aspect, scene identity in full, or general transform semantics.
The player/enemies occlude some reference letters. Their visible yellow-pixel bounds are not the full sign width or an overall fidelity score.
Neighboring-wall parallax, surface colors, shadows, sky, actors and HUD still differ. Materials are unlit/two-sided and collections 27/28 remain explicitly excluded.
This reference is ps2-native-recomp, not a hardware or PCSX2 cross-check. Prototype observations were not used.

comparisons.title: Retail street reference / candidate resource layout
comparisons.scenario: A repeatable first-fight retail snapshot alongside a Bevy overview of candidate r100 resources. Camera and exact scene association are not matched.
observations: Bevy now places ISO-backed terrain and buildings instead of showing only an isolated prop.
The first all-resource overview was dominated by sky resources; this inspection explicitly excludes collections 27 and 28.
The street-level reference and overhead candidate view are different viewpoints. This records the current gap, not a fidelity pass.
limits: No matched camera, runtime scene activation, original lighting/material state, actors, HUD or gameplay.
The reference is a third-party ps2-native-recomp rendering, not PS2 hardware or a PCSX2 cross-check.
The original reference PPM is preserved unchanged and downloadable. Its PNG is a lossless preview, not a substituted original.
The Bevy capture comes from an uncommitted development build using S -> R -> T hypotheses and an automatic bounds camera.
